candidates.name: Taiwanese Lu Rou Fan Pork Rice Bowls
candidates.why: Braised minced/diced pork ragu ladled over rice. Scales perfectly to a 14-serving pot and portions by weight. Source uses pork belly (no board id); swap to board-tracked pork shoulder ground or hand-diced keeps it budget and raises protein density. Confidence: source page publishes NO nutrition, so est_cal is my estimate for a shoulder-based build over 1 cup rice, not a verified number.

candidates.name: Sichuan Mapo Pork Rice Bowls
candidates.why: Simmered saucy skillet, no plating fuss, holds and reheats well. Tofu is the signature ingredient and has NO board home, so this only works if the pork ratio is pushed way up (roughly double the source's 8 oz pork per 6 servings). Confidence: source publishes 335 cal / 11g protein per serving WITHOUT rice and at a low pork ratio, so it fails the 25g bar as written; my est_cal/protein assumes a pork-forward rewrite over rice. Flag for the selector.

candidates.name: Cochinita Pibil Pork Rice Bowls
candidates.why: Slow-cooker shredded pork, the single most batch-friendly format there is, and achiote-paste is already a tracked commodity so the signature flavor maps cleanly. Genuinely distinct from the live carnitas and salsa verde pork bowls (citrus + annatto, not lard-crisped or tomatillo). Banana leaves are optional and get dropped. Confidence: source publishes no nutrition; est_cal is my estimate for shredded shoulder over rice and beans.

candidates.name: Kielbasa, Cabbage and Potato Skillet
candidates.why: Every single ingredient maps to a tracked commodity, which makes this one of the cheapest builds in the slice. One-pan skillet, scales linearly to 14 servings. Source publishes 508 cal / 20g protein per serving; protein needs a nudge (more kielbasa per pound of potato) to clear 25g, which is an easy rewrite lever.

candidates.name: Polish Bigos Pork and Kielbasa Stew
candidates.why: Sauerkraut and kielbasa are both tracked commodities and this is a true long-braise stew that gets better on day three, which is exactly the meal-prep use case. Source publishes 328 cal / 10g protein, which is far too lean on meat as written, so it needs a real pork shoulder addition to qualify. Confidence: est_cal/protein are my meat-forward rewrite, not the source's numbers. Prunes swap to tracked raisins.

candidates.name: Goan Pork Vindaloo Rice Bowls
candidates.why: Verified 766 cal / 47g protein per serving on the source page, the strongest protein-to-calorie number in this slice. Vinegar-and-garlic braise, cooks in one pot, tastes better reheated. Nothing like the live Indian entries (all chicken or ground beef keema). Spice base is nearly all tracked commodities; tamarind can be dropped for extra vinegar.

candidates.name: Vietnamese Thit Kho Braised Pork and Eggs
candidates.why: Caramel braise with hard-boiled eggs stirred in, which pushes protein up cheaply. Distinct from both live Vietnamese pork entries (those are grilled lemongrass chops and bun bowls). Source publishes 1,128 cal / 28g protein per serving at a 50/50 belly-shoulder ratio; going all pork shoulder cuts calories hard and lifts protein. Coconut soda swaps to tracked coconut milk plus sugar.

candidates.name: Japanese Butadon Pork Rice Bowls
candidates.why: Verified 408 cal / 29g protein for a half-pound-of-pork-across-two-bowls build, so the protein ratio is already right and only the portion needs scaling to clear 500 cal. Thin-sliced pork loin off a tracked cut, simmered in a soy-mirin glaze, weighed over rice. NOTE for the selector: this sits close to the Shogayaki candidate in this same slice (both thin pork loin + onion + soy over rice) — I kept both because the flavor axes differ (caramel-sweet vs ginger-forward) but they should be adjudicated as a pair.

candidates.name: Moo Shu Pork Rice Bowls
candidates.why: Classic take-out dish that is genuinely just a big cabbage-and-pork stir fry, so it scales to a 14-serving pan. Skip the pancakes and serve over rice, which is how it survives batch portioning. Cabbage and carrots are two of the cheapest tracked commodities. Source publishes 252 cal / 17g protein for filling only (no rice), so calories land in range once rice is added; protein needs a pork bump.

candidates.name: Sichuan Twice-Cooked Pork and Cabbage
candidates.why: The simmer-then-slice-then-stir-fry method is actually ideal for batch cooking: boil the whole pork piece once, slice, and finish in one pan. Source publishes 578 cal / 12g protein on a pure pork belly build, so this MUST be rewritten to pork shoulder to reach 25g protein. Confidence: my est numbers assume the shoulder swap, not the source's.

candidates.name: Ants Climbing a Tree Pork Noodles
candidates.why: One-pan saucy noodle dish, noodles absorb the sauce so it portions clean and reheats without drying. Source publishes 479 cal / 16g protein at a light 4 oz pork per 2 servings; doubling the ground pork gets it over the bar cheaply since ground-pork is a tracked commodity. Glass noodles have no exact board id (tracked rice-noodles is the nearest sub).

candidates.name: Beijing Zha Jiang Mian Pork Noodles
candidates.why: A meat sauce for noodles, which is the single most batch-friendly structure in the catalog (make sauce once, portion over noodles). Distinct from the live Dan Dan Noodles and Spicy Pork Noodles: this is a savory fermented-bean brown sauce with raw cucumber, not sesame or chili oil. Source publishes 410 cal / 7g protein for SAUCE ONLY on a pork belly build; needs ground pork and a bigger meat ratio. Confidence: est numbers are mine, not the source's. Two bean pastes have no board home.

candidates.name: Yu Xiang Shredded Pork Rice Bowls
candidates.why: Sweet-sour-garlicky shredded pork over rice, built on tracked pork tenderloin plus carrots and peppers. Source publishes 250 cal / 13.3g protein without rice at 8 oz pork for 4; needs roughly double the pork and a rice base to qualify. Confidence: my est numbers, not the source's. Wood ear and bamboo shoots drop out or sub to tracked mushrooms.

candidates.name: Pork Egg Roll in a Bowl
candidates.why: Every ingredient maps to a tracked commodity and cabbage plus ground pork is one of the cheapest protein-per-dollar combinations on the board. Single skillet, no assembly, portions by weight. Source publishes 372 cal / 22g protein with no starch; adding a rice base clears 500 cal and a modest pork bump clears 25g protein.

candidates.name: Asado de Puerco Chile Colorado Bowls
candidates.why: Verified 293 cal / 26g protein per serving on the source page, so the protein ratio already qualifies and rice plus beans carry it past 500 cal. A red-chile braise is a real gap in the live catalog, which has green chile, salsa verde, posole verde and tinga but no chile colorado. Dried chiles have no board id; tracked chili-powder plus tomato is the budget substitute.

candidates.name: Puerto Rican Pernil Rice Bowls
candidates.why: Slow cooker, a bone-in shoulder is one of the lowest cost-per-gram-of-protein items on the whole board, and the garlic-oregano rub is basically free. Distinct from live Cuban mojo pork (citrus-forward) and from carnitas. Source publishes no nutrition, so est_cal is my estimate for shredded shoulder over rice and beans. Sofrito and sazon have no board home but both are buildable from tracked onions, peppers, garlic, cilantro and spices.

candidates.name: Thai Basil Pork Pad Kra Pao Bowls
candidates.why: Verified 657 cal / 33g protein per serving on the source page, clears both bars as published. Fast ground-pork skillet, sauce is four tracked pantry bottles. Distinct from the live Thai pork entries (peanut tenderloin bowl and drunken noodles). Holy basil substitutes to tracked fresh-basil; Thai chilies sub to tracked jalapenos or red pepper flakes.

candidates.name: Hungarian Pork Goulash over Egg Noodles
candidates.why: Fully mapped ingredient list, every item is a tracked commodity including paprika and sour cream. Long simmer, one pot, reheats better than it starts. Source publishes 236 cal / 28g protein without the noodle base, so the protein ratio is already right and noodles carry it over 500 cal. Note for the selector: the live catalog has Hungarian Chicken Paprikash, so the sauce family overlaps even though the protein and dish name differ.

candidates.name: Pasta alla Norcina Creamy Sausage Pasta
candidates.why: Fully mapped, all eight ingredients are tracked commodities. Cream-and-sausage pasta holds and reheats well at 14 servings. Distinct from the live Italian Sausage Penne (that one is tomato and peppers, this is a white cream sauce with mushrooms). Source publishes 1,425 cal / 38g protein at a very rich 2-serving split, so calories come DOWN in a portioned rewrite while protein stays strong.

candidates.name: Louisiana Red Beans and Rice with Sausage
candidates.why: Verified 586 cal / 32g protein per serving on the source page, clears both bars as published. Dried beans plus smoked sausage is about as cheap as a high-protein dinner gets, and every component except andouille specifically maps to a tracked commodity (tracked kielbasa is the standard budget sub). Distinct from the live Cajun jambalaya and etouffee, which are both chicken.

candidates.name: Pork Chop and Stuffing Casserole
candidates.why: Fully mapped, and stuffing-mix, both cream soups and pork-chops are all tracked commodities, which makes this a very cheap 9x13. Source publishes 957 cal / 73g protein per serving, so it is protein-dense and the calories come down when portioned to 14. Distinct from the live cheesy pork chop hash brown casserole (different starch, different sauce).

candidates.name: Bangers and Mash with Onion Gravy
candidates.why: Fully mapped, every ingredient is a tracked commodity (tracked bratwurst stands in for British bangers). Sausages bake on a sheet pan while the mash and gravy go in bulk, so it scales to 14 without any per-plate work. Source publishes 666 cal / 36.4g protein per serving, clearing both bars as published. Nothing in the live catalog is a sausage-and-gravy plate.

candidates.name: Oven-Baked Pork Schnitzel with Potatoes
candidates.why: Fully mapped. Included specifically because it is the OVEN version on a wire rack, which is the only way a breaded cutlet survives batch cooking (fried-to-order does not scale). Source publishes no nutrition, so est_cal is my estimate for a 4 oz breaded loin chop plus roasted potatoes. Note for the selector: the live catalog has Pork Milanese with Roasted Potatoes, which is the same breaded-cutlet-plus-potato structure. This is the closest near-duplicate in my pool and I would drop it first if the count allows.

candidates.name: Spanish Chorizo and Chickpea Stew
candidates.why: Verified 619 cal / 25g protein per serving on the source page, right at both bars. One pot, chickpeas plus smoked sausage is cheap and the stew improves overnight. The one real gap is Spanish cured chorizo, which has NO board id at all (the live chorizo-and-potato-bowls recipe uses fresh Mexican chorizo, also unmapped) — closest tracked subs are kielbasa or italian-sausage plus extra paprika, which changes the dish. Flagging honestly.

candidates.name: Pork Fried Rice Bowls
candidates.why: Fully mapped, all eleven ingredients are tracked commodities. Verified 318 cal / 25g protein per serving on the source page, so the protein ratio is already at the bar and only portion size needs scaling to clear 500 cal. Big-batch fried rice is standard restaurant practice, so 14 servings is realistic. Distinct protein from the live ground-beef fried rice.

candidates.name: Sausage Hash Brown Breakfast Casserole
candidates.why: Fully mapped, every ingredient is a tracked commodity including hash-browns and evaporated-milk. Verified 474 cal / 25g protein per serving on the source page. A 9x13 egg bake is the definition of weigh-and-divide portioning, and breakfast-for-dinner is an unfilled gap in the live catalog. Eggs plus sausage is a very cheap protein pairing.

candidates.name: Indonesian Babi Kecap Pork Rice Bowls
candidates.why: Sweet soy braise, one pot, shreds and portions cleanly. Fills an Indonesian gap the catalog does not touch at all. Kecap manis has no board id but is just tracked soy-sauce plus brown-sugar reduced, which is the standard budget build. Source publishes 653 cal / 11g protein on a pork belly build; the shoulder swap is mandatory to hit 25g. Confidence: est numbers are my rewrite, not the source's.

candidates.name: Chinese Pork and Green Bean Stir-Fry Bowls
candidates.why: Nearly fully mapped; fresh-green-beans and oyster-sauce are both tracked. Velveted pork plus one vegetable over rice, which portions by weight without fuss. Source publishes 210 cal / 13g protein without rice at 12 oz pork for 4, so this needs roughly double the pork plus a rice base. Confidence: est numbers are mine. Note for the selector: this is one of three single-vegetable Chinese pork stir-fries in my pool (green bean, onion, ginger-carrot) — they differ by sauce and vegetable but should be adjudicated together.

candidates.name: Chuletas Guisadas Stewed Pork Chops and Rice
candidates.why: Verified 516 cal / 52g protein per serving on the source page — the best protein-per-calorie ratio in the whole slice — and the source publishes a $3.84/serving cost, which confirms budget-buildable. Braised chops in a tomato-sofrito gravy, one pot, holds beautifully. Distinct from the live Southern smothered chops (cream/onion gravy, not tomato-adobo). Sofrito and sazon are buildable from tracked produce and spices.

candidates.name: Irish Dublin Coddle Sausage and Potatoes
candidates.why: Fully mapped, every ingredient is tracked including bratwurst and bacon. Source publishes 577 cal / 20g protein and a $2.26/serving cost. Low-and-slow oven pot that only gets better on reheat, and 14 servings is just a bigger dutch oven. Protein needs a modest sausage bump to clear 25g. Nothing Irish in the live catalog.

candidates.name: Filipino Pork Menudo Rice Bowls
candidates.why: Verified 389 cal / 33g protein per serving on the source page before rice, so the protein ratio clears comfortably and rice pushes calories over 500. Tomato-braised pork with potato, carrot and chickpeas is all tracked commodities. Distinct from the two live Filipino pork entries (adobo and giniling). Beef liver is traditional but optional and gets dropped; annatto subs to tracked achiote-paste.

candidates.name: Japanese Pork Nikujaga Potato Stew
candidates.why: Simmered pot stew, the source explicitly states pork is the standard eastern-Japan version. Potatoes, onions and carrots are three of the cheapest tracked commodities. Source publishes 338 cal / 17g protein per serving, so it needs a pork increase and a rice base to qualify. Confidence: est numbers are mine. Dashi subs to tracked chicken-broth; shirataki gets dropped.

candidates.name: Roast Pork Lo Mein Noodle Bowls
candidates.why: Tossed noodle bowl, holds and reheats well at volume. Note for the selector: the source builds it on char siu roast pork and the live catalog already has Slow Cooker Char Siu Pork Bowls, so the pork prep overlaps even though the dish (noodles + vegetables) is different; the live lo mein entries are chicken and ground turkey. Source publishes NO nutrition, so est_cal is entirely my estimate. Several Chinese pantry vegetables have no board home and would sub to tracked cabbage, carrots and mushrooms.

candidates.name: Pork Ginger Carrot Rice Bowls
candidates.why: Nearly fully mapped and built on two of the cheapest tracked items on the board, ground-pork and carrots. Genuinely a one-pan meal designed as a rice bowl, so it needs zero adaptation for the format. Source publishes 404 cal / 21g protein without rice; a small pork bump plus the rice base clears both bars. See the note on the green-bean stir-fry candidate about the three single-vegetable pork stir-fries in this pool.

candidates.name: Italian Sausage and Broccoli Pasta
candidates.why: Fully mapped, every ingredient is a tracked commodity, and the source publishes a $0.90/serving cost which makes it one of the cheapest builds in the slice. No tomato or cream sauce, just garlic-chili oil, which keeps it distinct from the live Italian Sausage Penne. Source publishes 403 cal / 18g protein; a sausage increase from a half pound to a full pound clears both bars.

candidates.name: Greek Pork Souvlaki Rice Bowls
candidates.why: Verified 391.7 cal / 36.2g protein per serving on the source page, so the protein ratio is excellent and the rice base carries calories over 500. Marinated pork cubes roast on a sheet pan in bulk (skip the skewers, which are the only non-scaling part). Note for the selector: the live catalog has Chicken Souvlaki Rice Bowls, so the marinade and bowl structure overlap even though the protein differs.

candidates.name: Chinese Pork and Onion Stir-Fry Bowls
candidates.why: Nearly fully mapped and dirt cheap: the only vegetable is onions, one of the lowest-cost tracked commodities, and the sauce leans on tracked ketchup and worcestershire. Source publishes 234 cal / 20g protein without rice at 12 oz pork for 4; more pork plus the rice base clears both bars. See the green-bean candidate's note about the three single-vegetable pork stir-fries.

candidates.name: Ham and Potato Cheddar Casserole
candidates.why: Fully mapped, all eight ingredients are tracked commodities. Source publishes 462 cal / 23g protein per serving, both just under the bars and both easily lifted by increasing the ham. A 9x13 bake portions by weight. Ham is a protein the catalog does not use anywhere in 213 live recipes, which makes this a real category gap rather than a variation.

candidates.name: Japanese Ginger Pork Shogayaki Bowls
candidates.why: Verified 361 cal / 40g protein per serving on the source page, the second-best protein ratio in the slice, and the rice base carries it over 500 cal. Nearly fully mapped; only sake is unhoused. NOTE for the selector: this is the paired near-duplicate with the Butadon candidate above (both thin pork loin + onion + soy over rice). They differ by ginger-forward vs caramel-sweet and by the shredded cabbage side, but if only one survives, this one has the stronger published protein number.

candidates.name: Buta Kimchi Pork and Kimchi Rice Bowls
candidates.why: Fast one-pan stir fry that scales, and kimchi does a lot of flavor work for very little cost per serving. Distinct from the three live Korean pork entries, which are all gochujang or soy-braised with no fermented cabbage. Kimchi has NO board id, which is the main risk here — it is a specialty-aisle buy, not a tracked commodity. Confidence: source publishes NO nutrition at all, so est_cal and the protein assumption are entirely mine, based on a shoulder swap off the source's pork belly.
